correctness.rationale: An exact Fourier basis gives lambda_k=2 cos(phi+2 pi k/n) with lambda_(k+n/2)=-lambda_k. Balanced eigenfrequency relations characterize PGST after quotienting global phase via continuous-time Kronecker. Antipodal necessity follows from four-index relations. Odd-prime coset sums give an incompatible odd relation for every flux. Their phase products, a triangle inequality and Cauchy-Schwarz prove the uniform amplitude gap 1/(pn). For n=2^r and transcendental tan(phi), algebraicity forces all relations to be vanishing cyclotomic polynomials, hence equal coefficient halves and antipodal phase compatibility. Two Fourier eigenvalue pairs rule out PST since transcendental tangent cannot equal a rational ratio. At phi=pi/n, equal-eigenvalue opposite-parity terms exactly cancel. Finite standalone checks of Fourier modes, polynomial/parity identities, uniform gap and dark channel were performed; they do not prove infinite limits.

value.rationale: Uniform magnetic Peierls hopping is a natural physical modification of a tight-binding ring. This result gives all even orders a sharp odd-prime/no-transfer dichotomy and proves robust PGST for almost all fluxes at power-of-two orders, while distinguishing approximate from exact transport. The flux-independent quantitative gap is a substantive exact obstruction. A specifically dark half-flux supplies a physically motivated boundary to the generic statement; no claim of optimal error bound or algebraic-exception classification is made.
